minutes.headline: Zoning board granted two special permits: a 15-foot side-yard reduction for a solar array and a front setback for a garage.
minutes.summary: The Zoning Board of Appeals heard two applications. It modified a January special permit so a ground-mount solar array at 355 Northfield Road can sit ten feet from the side line and be one array instead of two. It then granted a special permit for a two-car garage and workshop at 129 Peninsula Drive with a reduced front setback.

what_happened.line: The Zoning Board of Appeals granted a modification of a January special permit, reducing the side-yard setback for a ground-mount solar array at 355 Northfield Road.
The modification also changes the project from two solar arrays to one.
The January conditions on fencing and boulders stay in place; only the setback and the number of arrays change.
The board granted a special permit for a two-car garage and workshop at 129 Peninsula Drive with a reduced front setback.
The applicant said moving the driveway instead of the array would cost thousands of dollars. Vote counts were not audible; both grants were stated as granted.

why_it_matters: Setback relief lets buildings and solar arrays sit closer to property lines than the zoning bylaw normally allows, so neighbors on Northfield Road and Peninsula Drive may see the change at their boundary.
The January conditions on fencing and boulders were kept, so the screening that abutters were promised still applies to the solar site.
